segments: Bill picket was a pioneering
African-American cowboy and wild west
showman born in 1870 in Travis County
Texas to formerly enslaved parents
picket grew up on a ranch and learned
the skills of a cowboy at an early age
he became famous for inventing the rodeo
technique of bulldogging which involved
wrestling steers To The Ground by biting
their upper lip a method inspired by
observing how dogs controlled cattle his
bulldogging act became a main attraction
captivating audiences across the United
States Canada Mexico and even Europe
Bill picket daring stunts and exeptional
Rodeo skills earned him widespread
Acclaim and he was often referred to as
the Dusky demon he was the first black
cowboy to gain widespread recognition in
the rodeo circuit breaking racial
barriers in the process his legacy was
cemented postumus when he became the
first African-American inducted into the
national Cowboy Hall of Fame Bill
Pickett's name is still celebrated in
cowboy history and several rodeos
schools and events are named in his
honor including the bill picket
Invitational Rodeo which is dedicated to
promoting black cowboy culture
